statement:
Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel sigma algebra, including dimension zero. Let V:E->R, alpha,beta>=0 and eta in R. Assume alpha>0, alpha<=beta, V is C2, alpha||v||^2<=D2V(x)[v,v]<=beta||v||^2 for every x,v in E, eta>0 and beta*eta<=1.
For y,r in E put c=y-eta grad V(r), h_r(x)=grad V(x)-grad V(r), R(x,p)=(x,-p),
Phi_(y,r,u)(x,p)=(c+cos(u)(x-c)+sqrt(eta)sin(u)p, -sin(u)/sqrt(eta)(x-c)+cos(u)p),
S_r(x,p)=(x,p-(2<p,h_r(x)>/||h_r(x)||^2)h_r(x)). Real division by zero is zero, so a zero normal gives the identity bounce. Let ell=volume_E tensor volume_E, with canonical Hilbert-space Lebesgue measure.
For every integer n>=0 and horizon T>=0, let Delta_n(T) consist of real tuples 0<t_0<...<t_(n-1)<T. Equivalently, prepending 0 produces a strictly increasing tuple and every entry is less than T. Let Prefix_n(T) be this subtype and m_n,T the comap of Lebesgue measure on R^n under its inclusion. This is unnormalized simplex volume. For n=0 the tuple is empty and its zero-dimensional volume is one; for T=0 and n>0 the subtype is empty.
Write q_0=0 and q_(j+1)=t_j. Starting at z_0=z, define z_(j+1)=S_r(Phi_(y,r,t_j-q_j)(z_j)) for 0<=j<n. Define records K_j=(q_j,z_j), each embedded in the live branch of (R_nonnegative x (E x E)) plus a cemetery symbol. For a general history of n+1 such records, the path reconstruction Psi at s in [0,T] starts from z and visits records in increasing index order: a live record (a,w) replaces the accumulator by Phi_(y,r,s-a)(w) exactly when a<=s; future records and cemetery records leave it unchanged. Here s-a is nonnegative subtraction. Define Gamma_(y,r,z,t)=Psi(K), the actual finite prescribed path; thus its value at an event is the post-bounce value. Let A_(y,r)(z,t)=Gamma_(y,r,z,t)(T).
Define the actual positive-part event rate lambda_r(x,p)=sqrt(eta) max(0,<p,grad V(x)-grad V(r)>), and the target energy U_y(x,p)=V(x)+||x-y||^2/(2 eta)+||p||^2/2. The rate after momentum reversal is lambda_r(R(x,p)); it is evaluated on the same trajectory, not on a reversed-time trajectory.
For every y,r,z,n,T,t as above, extend the actual prescribed path to real s by gamma(s)=Gamma(min(max(s,0),T)), with the argument understood as the nonnegative closed-interval subtype. Put A=Gamma(T), Iplus=integral from 0 to T of lambda_r(gamma(s)) ds, and Iminus=integral from 0 to T of lambda_r(R(gamma(s))) ds, both with real Lebesgue measure. Both integrands are interval integrable. The exact identities are
U_y(A)-U_y(z)=Iplus-Iminus,
exp(-U_y(z)) exp(-Iplus)=exp(-U_y(A)) exp(-Iminus).
All finite event counts n>=0, horizons T>=0, rank-zero spaces and zero reflection normals are included. No positive jump-rate condition is imposed on the prescribed tuple. No measurability, integrability, energy identity or normalizing-constant premise is added to the six source assumptions. The simplex measure m is retained to preserve the existing path interface but is not used by these two scalar identities. The weights here are unnormalized; a common Gibbs normalizer would cancel but existence of the normalized stationary law is a separate obligation.
This is the actual finite prescribed-path energy and Gibbs/survival identity in the Appendix A.1 reversal proof. It does not assert reversed-event density matching, pointwise time reversal at right-continuous jump values, weighted sector preservation, stationary averaging or invariant probability laws, restart/Markovness, hypocoercivity, implementation errors, expected oracle cost, main sampling results or actual-input composition.
